front.title: Consequence-Bound Execution Authority for Autonomous Systems: Operation Reconstruction, Independent Validation, and Protected Effectuation Profiles

abstract.t:
Authorization to compute, propose, prepare, simulate or request an operation is not, by itself, authorization to cause the operation's actual consequential effect. An authorized operation may afterwards be transformed, delegated, delayed, replicated, compiled, offloaded or executed under different technical conditions. This document describes an architecture, and a set of candidate interoperability requirements, for separating those authorizations: a proposed operation is held as a Candidate Act in a Non-Effective State; the Actual Pending Operation is reconstructed; current source authority, context, dependencies and policy and revocation epochs are evaluated by an independent validator; a scoped, non-bearer execution authorization is issued; and a protected Finality Sink at the actual effectuation boundary re-derives the operation, enforces the authorization, and supports reconciliation against authoritative outcome evidence.
The document is an individual, informational technical proposal. It credits OAuth, JWT/CWT, RBAC/ABAC, zero-trust, remote attestation, transaction logs, hardware isolation and cryptographic signatures for their established functions and does not characterize them as defective. It includes a threat model, 12 figures, 39 consequence- specific profiles, a non-normative European applicability discussion and an examiner-oriented terminology appendix. It is not an IETF standard, an EU regulatory instrument, a telecommunications or financial standard, or an endorsement by any named company.
